outcome: As of the latest material found (Fu's arXiv preprint of 3 Apr 2026, v2 1 Aug 2026; Miller's Ohio State talk of 13 Jan 2026; the 2025 survey arXiv 2509.18025, v2 1 Jun 2026), the question is still open: the only new work on it since 26 Jan 2024 is a conditional theorem (Fu, 2026) that an analytic trans-exponential function added to R_an,exp gives an o-minimal, trans-exponential structure provided the function satisfies a regularity assumption that the paper calls necessary for o-minimality and that I could not see verified for any function; no AI system is credited with any part of it.
problem_asks: Read against the statement alone. (1) The existence of an o-minimal first-order theory. The statement names no language and no ambient structure. (2) That this theory has a trans-exponential function: a function that is eventually at least exp_n(t) for every n >= 1, where exp_1 is the exponential and exp_(n+1) is exp composed with exp_n. The statement's gloss is 'rapid growth'. Both parts must hold together: an o-minimal theory and, in it, a trans-exponential function. Points the statement does not settle: (a) whether the function must be definable in the theory, or merely a function in its models; (b) whether exp must be in the language, since 'trans-exponential' is measured against exp. The literature reads the question as: is there an o-minimal expansion of the real field in which some definable unary function eventually dominates every iterated exponential (van den Dries and Miller; Bareilles et al. Open Question 3.33). I use that reading for the events below.

events.what_happened: Adele Padgett, 'Sublogarithmic-transexponential series', arXiv:2211.06736 (math.LO, 78 pages), later also her thesis of the same title (search excerpt gives advisor Thomas Scanlon and an escholarship.org record; not opened). Builds an ordered differential field of sublogarithmic-transexponential series, adapting the van den Dries–Macintyre–Marker logarithmic-exponential transseries. Proves that germs at +infinity of one-variable terms in a language L_transexp (an exponential language extended by a transexponential function E, its derivatives and compositional inverses) are ordered, hence a transexponential Hardy field closed under composition. The candidate structure R_transexp is proposed; the thesis says that quantifier elimination for R_transexp would give o-minimality, and that QE is not proved.
events.revisions: v1 12 Nov 2022 (arXiv abstract page opened; no later version noted in what I read).
events.delivers: Establishes that the germs at +infinity of one-variable terms in the candidate language L_transexp are ordered, so they form a Hardy field, and that this Hardy field is closed under composition and contains a transexponential function. Restricted to germs of terms in one variable. It does not show that any o-minimal structure exists, that R_transexp is o-minimal, or that any definable function in an o-minimal structure is trans-exponential. It is a Hardy-field analogue of the candidate, not an o-minimal result.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks. The step that would give o-minimality (quantifier elimination for R_transexp) is not proved; the thesis itself says so.
events.doubts: The o-minimality programme relies on QE, which is open per the paper. The Hardy-field result is evidence, not proof, as the author says in the thesis abstract. Not reviewed in any journal I could find. The Padgett–Bagayoko–Kaplan follow-up using Lion's criterion (2023 talk abstracts) did not surface as a paper.
events.direction: Neutral toward the question. It supplies a candidate and evidence (a Hardy field containing a transexponential function) but no o-minimal structure; if the candidate's QE holds, the answer is yes.
events.object: A transexponential Hardy field of sublogarithmic-transexponential series, closed under composition, and germs of R_transexp-terms forming an ordered set. Not an explicit function on R; it is the algebraic construction of germs. The transexponential E itself is not given as a closed formula in what I read.

events.what_happened: Chris Miller, unpublished note 'Re-examination of an old question' on his Ohio State page (qpole.pdf), dated 7 Feb 2023 in a search excerpt, which says it is not a preprint. The note asks whether an o-minimal expansion of (Q,<,+) can define a unary function mapping a bounded set onto an unbounded set. It proves: if so, then some o-minimal expansion of the real field is not exponentially bounded. The note says the antecedent is widely believed false. The PDF could not be opened (binary); the date and content come from search excerpts only.
events.delivers: Conditional only. If an o-minimal expansion of (Q,<,+) defines a unary function from a bounded set onto an unbounded set, then some o-minimal expansion of R is not exponentially bounded: a definable unary function f with no exp_n dominating it (eventually f > exp_n for every n in an o-minimal setting), which is a trans-exponential function in the problem's sense. Unconditionally, nothing. The antecedent is stated by the author to be open.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks, unconditionally. The antecedent (a bounded-to-unbounded function over (Q,<,+)) is open per the note and per Miller's 2026 talk.
events.doubts: (1) The note is explicitly unpublished and not submitted (search excerpt of the note and of a folklore citation). (2) A related Miller document is cited in search excerpts for the claim that the Pfaffian closure of (R,<,+,exp,*) is not exponentially bounded (see disputes). The excerpts disagree on whether that claim is in this note or in his two-group notes (tg.pdf); neither PDF could be opened.
events.direction: Toward yes, conditional on an open antecedent. It does not produce a structure.

events.what_happened: Lothar Sebastian Krapp and Salma Kuhlmann, 'Ordered transexponential fields', arXiv:2305.04607 (math.LO, math.AC), 26 pages. Develops a first-order theory of ordered fields with an exponential e and a transexponential T satisfying T(x+1) = e(T(x)) for positive x. Describes the archimedean models, gives necessary and sufficient conditions on the value group of an ordered exponential field for a compatible transexponential to exist, and classifies countable ordered transexponential fields by valuation-theoretic invariants. Published in Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 176(4), 103541 (2025), DOI 10.1016/j.apal.2024.103541 (from a search excerpt; not opened). The arXiv abstract page was opened; the paper body was not.
events.revisions: v1 8 May 2023; v2 21 Jul 2023 (arXiv abstract page). Journal version APAL 2025 (search excerpt).
events.delivers: A first-order axiomatisation and classification of ordered transexponential fields (fields with e and T). Not a statement about o-minimal structures: the abstract page mentions no o-minimality result. It does not show that any o-minimal structure defines a transexponential function, and it is not an o-minimal theory of R. It is an algebraic analogue.

checked_by.qualification: Journal of record in mathematical logic; accepted the paper for publication
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in APAL 176(4), 2025 (per search excerpt; not verified against the journal page)

events.direction: Neutral; not a claim about the question as stated.

events.what_happened: Matthias Aschenbrenner, Lou van den Dries and Joris van der Hoeven, 'The theory of maximal Hardy fields', arXiv:2408.05232, submitted 2 Aug 2024. Abstract: all maximal Hardy fields are elementarily equivalent as differential fields to the differential field T of transseries, with applications. The 2025 survey arXiv 2509.18025 says maximal Hardy fields are necessarily transexponential, citing this family of results; that sentence is not in the abstract I read.
events.revisions: v1 2 Aug 2024 only, per the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: A model-theoretic statement about maximal Hardy fields as differential fields. It is about Hardy fields of germs, not about o-minimal structures or about any structure that defines a function. It bears on the question only as the Hardy-field side of the analogy. It does not produce an o-minimal structure with a trans-exponential definable function.
events.doubts: Not relevant to the o-minimal question as stated; recorded because it is a neighbouring result inside the window. I did not open the full text.

events.what_happened: Chris Miller, talk 'Tameness and transexponentialism', Ohio State Logic Seminar, Tuesday 13 Jan 2026, Dulles Hall 027. Abstract (per the event page; quoted in part): the talk concerns 'whether there exist o-minimal expansions of the real field that are not exponentially bounded', and states that 'three and a half decades after first being posed, the question is still open'. It also discusses whether an o-minimal expansion of (Q,<,+) can define a unary function mapping a bounded set onto an unbounded set. No slides, notes or preprint found.
events.delivers: No result. A public statement by the author that the question (whether an o-minimal expansion of R that is not exponentially bounded exists) is still open in January 2026.
events.doubts: The talk's status claim sits uneasily with the Pfaffian-closure claim in Miller's notes (see disputes). The abstract does not say which is right.
events.direction: Neutral; it states the question open.

events.what_happened: Yayi Fu, 'Towards Trans-Exponential O-minimal Expansion of (R,+,·,0,1,<)', arXiv:2604.03477 (math.LO). Adds an analytic trans-exponential function phi to R_an,exp, the real analytic exponential field. The introduction says that none of the known structures R, R_exp, R_log, R_an,exp has a definable trans-exponential function. Theorem 1.1 (per the html v2 text): 'Suppose that phi is an analytic trans-exponential function satisfying the regularity assumption in Theorem 2.8. Then R_an,exp,phi is o-minimal and trans-exponential.' The paper says the regularity assumption (a triangulation of a certain set with local finiteness) is a necessary condition for o-minimality, so the result is a reduction: o-minimality of R_an,exp,phi reduces to the existence of 'many' regular values for certain definable systems of functions. Method per secondary summaries: Wilkie's o-minimality test, an analytic function satisfying an Abel equation (the paper cites Kneser's 1950 analytic solution psi of psi(e^x) = psi(x) + 1), and Milnor's method. The abstract page's own wording: 'We add an analytic trans-exponential function phi to R_an,exp. We reduce the o-minimality of R_an,exp,phi to the existence of many regular values for some definable systems of functions.'
events.revisions: v1 3 Apr 2026 21:53:54 UTC (22 KB); v2 1 Aug 2026 21:53:52 UTC (22 KB), the current version per arXiv abstract page. I did not identify what changed between v1 and v2.
events.delivers: Conditional. For the expansion of R_an,exp by a single analytic trans-exponential function phi that satisfies the regularity assumption of Theorem 2.8, the structure is o-minimal and trans-exponential, i.e. it defines a function eventually dominating every iterated exponential. That would answer the question yes in the reading used here. Restrictions: (a) one added analytic function; (b) the regularity assumption, which the paper says is necessary for o-minimality; (c) whether any particular phi meets it is not shown in what I read.
events.remains: (a) Whether any analytic trans-exponential phi satisfies the regularity assumption of Theorem 2.8, which is the whole content left once the theorem's conditional is granted. (b) Anything about other o-minimal theories or structures not of the form R_an,exp with one added phi. (c) Whether the regularity assumption is verified; the paper's title ('Towards') and the search summaries both describe it as a partial step.
events.doubts: (1) No journal publication, referee report or published critique found. (2) The o-minimality conclusion is conditional on the regularity assumption, which the paper calls necessary for o-minimality, so verifying it for a given phi is the remaining task. I could read the html v2 only up to about 100,000 of about 111,700 characters, and I did not see a verification. (3) Secondary summaries disagree on method: a search excerpt says Milnor's method; the emergentmind summary says Morse theory and homological methods. Neither was checked against the paper's text. (4) The relation to the Padgett–Bagayoko–Kaplan Lion-criterion project (2023 talks) is unknown. (5) The emergentmind summary is automated and the author of the summary is unknown.
events.direction: Toward yes, conditionally: an o-minimal trans-exponential expansion of R_an,exp by phi exists if phi meets the regularity assumption, and the paper calls that assumption necessary for o-minimality, so the existence question reduces to a checkable property of phi.
events.object: An analytic function phi: R -> R, trans-exponential (eventually above every iterate of exp), added to R_an,exp as a new function symbol. The paper's Theorem 1.1 is stated for any phi satisfying the regularity assumption, so the object is a class of functions rather than a single explicit function. Per the search excerpts, phi is tied to an Abel-type equation and to Kneser's 1950 analytic solution, but I could not confirm from the text which phi is used, whether it is explicit, or whether the regularity assumption holds for it. Not checkable by hand from what I read.

disputes.summary: Miller's notes, as quoted in search excerpts, state that the Pfaffian closure of (R,<,+,exp,*) is not exponentially bounded and is o-minimal by Speissegger (1999), citing Miller and Speissegger (JSL 2002), and call a related reduct claim unpublished folklore (cites [4, Proposition 1]). If the Pfaffian-closure claim is right, it gives a trans-exponential definable function in an o-minimal expansion of R, i.e. a yes answer, decades before the 2024-2026 work. The same author's 2026 talk says the question is still open; the 2003 Miller–Starchenko status note (search excerpt) says every known o-minimal expansion of R is exponentially bounded; Fu's introduction and the 2025 survey say the same. I could not open the notes, so I cannot tell which document carries the claim or what its context is. Not resolved here.

The emergentmind open-problem page cites this question as Open Question 3.31 of arXiv 2509.18025. The html v2 text of that survey labels it Open Question 3.33 ('Does there exist an o-minimal structure which defines a transexponential function?'). The survey attributes the question to no one by name in the text read. Attribution to van den Dries and Miller (1996) and to Marker and Miller (1997, difference equation f(x+1)=e^{f(x)}) comes from secondary sources (search excerpts) and was not checked against those works.

summary: I ran 45 standard-mode web searches and opened about twenty sources (listed below), including the arXiv abstract pages for each preprint, the html v2 text of Fu's preprint and of the 2025 survey arXiv 2509.18025, Miller's seminar and directory pages, the Wikipedia article O-minimal theory (last edited 1 Oct 2026, which mentions the problem nowhere), and two 2020 papers that do not contain the claim I was looking for. Miller's notes (tg.pdf and qpole.pdf) and Speissegger's and Miller–Speissegger's papers could not be read: the fetch tool returns binary PDFs and Bash needed approval, so I could not run a text extractor. The events are these. Pre-window: Padgett (Nov 2022) builds a transexponential Hardy field and proves the germs of candidate terms ordered, leaving quantifier elimination, and so o-minimality, open; Miller (7 Feb 2023, unpublished, date from a search excerpt) shows that a bounded-to-unbounded function over (Q,<,+) would give a non-exponentially-bounded o-minimal expansion of R, with the antecedent open; Krapp and Kuhlmann (May 2023) axiomatise ordered transexponential fields, which is algebra and not o-minimality. In-window: Aschenbrenner, van den Dries and van der Hoeven (2 Aug 2024) on maximal Hardy fields, which is about Hardy fields and not o-minimal structures. Post-window: Miller's talk (13 Jan 2026) says the question is still open; Fu's preprint (3 Apr 2026, v2 1 Aug 2026) proves that R_an,exp expanded by an analytic trans-exponential phi is o-minimal and trans-exponential provided phi satisfies a regularity assumption (Theorem 2.8), which the paper calls necessary for o-minimality. That is the only substantive new event. I found no verification that any phi meets the assumption, no journal publication, and no critique. The judgment about how much this settles is for the second pass. The question's status as of Oct 2026 rests on the conditional nature of Fu's theorem, the 2025 survey, and Miller's 2026 talk. The main unresolved tension is the Pfaffian-closure claim in Miller's notes, which would answer the question yes in a structure dating to around 1999-2002 if it holds, and which conflicts with every other source I read, including Miller's own 2026 abstract; I could not check it. On the AI question, I found no AI system credited with anything in any event. The AI-specific searches (lab announcements, AI-math trackers, Lean repositories, and combined model-name queries) turned up nothing on this question. OpenAI's Astra announcement of 1 Aug 2026 lists ten results, none in model theory, according to a secondary write-up (the primary OpenAI page returned HTTP 403). The one AI-disclosed math.LO-adjacent paper I saw (arXiv 2609.23015, Lean-formalised bit pigeonhole bounds, credits GPT-6 Astra and Claude models) is complexity theory, not this question. Fu's visible text (acknowledgements thank Lou van den Dries) discloses no AI tool, and I did not read the full text. Where a call was close: Fu's result counts as a yes only if the regularity assumption holds for some phi; I could not confirm that, and the paper's own 'Towards' title and conditional theorem suggest the authors did not claim it. Padgett's result is an analogue and I have discounted it. The Pfaffian-closure claim is the only item that could move the answer to yes without a new 2024-2026 event, and it is not established.
competing_reading: The strongest case for yes: Fu's theorem gives an o-minimal, trans-exponential expansion of R_an,exp, and the paper's regularity assumption may well hold for a natural choice of phi (the paper calls it necessary for o-minimality, which is a strong hint that the authors expect to verify it). Separately, if Miller's Pfaffian-closure claim is correct, the question has been answered yes since the Pfaffian closure of R_exp (Speissegger 1999, o-minimal) was shown not to be exponentially bounded, and the 2026 status statements would be wrong. The strongest case for no-change or still-open: the 2025 survey, Miller's own January 2026 talk, and the paper's own 'Towards' title all treat the question as open; the conditional theorem is not an answer until phi is shown to satisfy the assumption. A third reading, on the statement's wording: 'o-minimal first order theory' might be meant to include o-minimal theories of structures not expanding R, for which the growth comparison against exp is undefined unless exp is in the language, which would make the question a different one; I have not researched that reading beyond noting it.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A verification that some analytic trans-exponential phi satisfies the regularity assumption of Theorem 2.8 in Fu's paper, or a referee report or journal version of the paper that checks it. (2) The text of Miller's notes tg.pdf and qpole.pdf, to see which document contains the Pfaffian-closure claim, its Proposition 1, and its citations, together with the text of Miller–Speissegger (JSL 2002) and Speissegger (Crelle 1999) for the exponential-boundedness claim. (3) A statement from Miller or Speissegger reconciling the Pfaffian-closure claim with the 2003 status note and the 2026 talk. (4) The Padgett–Bagayoko–Kaplan Lion-criterion work, if it is posted. (5) Confirmation of the intended reading of the Wikipedia bullet: definable function in an o-minimal expansion of R, versus a more general o-minimal theory.
